analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: Democrats made significant gains in the midterms, and multiple outlets project they win both the House and the Senate. The NYT needle points to a 55-45 Senate majority, which would be 8 gains.

AP count in the House is 205-123 Democratic with 218 needed, 22 pickups so far versus 3 required for the majority. CNN and NBC already project a Democratic House win. AP Senate count is 52-41, with Democratic pickups projected in NC, SC, OH, KS, IA and TX.

Divided government adds constraints on the Trump administration: all legislation, spending packages to avoid a shutdown and debt ceiling increases need some Democratic votes. The Senate could block Cabinet, Supreme Court and Fed Governor appointments. Trump keeps a veto that needs two-thirds of both chambers to override.

Market reaction: S&P 500 futures were down 0.42% and Nasdaq 100 futures down 0.49% this morning, after being down more than 1% earlier. The selloff is led by tech, partly on expectations of tougher AI regulation under Democratic control.

Treasuries rallied on the view that divided government makes fiscal stimulus harder to pass. The 2yr yield fell 3.5bps overnight to 4.60% and the 10yr fell 2.9bps to 4.94%. Fed hikes priced by the June 2027 meeting fell 3.3bps to 55bps and the dollar index fell 0.40%.

In Asia, tech-exposed indices fell sharply before recovering. The Nikkei is down 2.09%, and the KOSPI is flat (+0.03%) after being down more than 4% at the lows. The Hang Seng (+0.89%), CSI 300 (+1.02%) and Shanghai Comp (+0.83%) gained.

Before the results, oil fell as Iran's President Pezeshkian said the Supreme Leader granted 'additional authority' for talks on previously non-negotiable issues. Qatari mediators expected US and Iran feedback on a new proposal within 36 hours. Brent fell 1.12% to $103.60/bbl and European gas fell 3.44% to €91.60/MWh.

Caution persisted: Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary said the US response was not satisfactory, and Iranian state TV said no new developments had been reached on an agreement. Oil recovered from its lows.
The S&P 500 rose 0.36% after 3 straight declines. The Nasdaq gained 0.83% and the Philly semiconductor index gained 2.63% after falling 11.6% over the prior three sessions.
US data stayed resilient. September JOLTS openings rose to 7.523m vs 7.164m expected, the quits rate hit a 15-month high of 2.1%, and September factory orders rose 1.8% vs 1.2% expected.
Futures raised the probability of a December Fed hike from 74% to 78% by the close. The 2yr yield rose 3.6bps to 4.63% and the 10yr rose 5.1bps to 4.96%.

ECB hike pricing for December rose from 83% to 89% after comments from Radev, Nagel and Kocher. 10yr Bund yields rose 3.8bps, OATs 5.1bps and BTPs 3.8bps. The STOXX 600 fell 0.58%, and STOXX 600 futures are down another 0.66%.
Day ahead: Euro Area October flash CPI, US ISM services, ADP private payrolls and the September trade balance. ECB's Lane and Moulin speak. Qualcomm, McDonald's and Uber report earnings.

sector_views.rationale: Tech led the futures selloff on expectations that Democratic control could bring tougher AI regulation, but futures pared losses from over -1% to about -0.4%.

earnings_insights: Qualcomm, McDonald's and Uber are scheduled to report earnings on the day the note was published. No estimates are given.
